column1: # boru Language Specification: the boru:tui module (Tier-1 words)
# Loadable module of raw-terminal words (design/TUI.0.md §4). They are
# reached only after `import`, under the `Tui` namespace:
#   Tui.open       — take the terminal over via the registered backend
#   Tui.read-event — next decoded input event ({within: ms} → None on deadline)
#   Tui.print-at   — styled text into the offscreen grid
#   Tui.show       — present the grid to the terminal
# The spec harness registers NO terminal backend (there is no TTY on CI),
# so `open` pins the first-class no-backend error and every other word
# pins its wrong-handle rejection; live happy paths run in Go against
# module-net.tsv leaves live sockets to Go.
# §3  the Terminal handle type is exported as a type literal

column3: Terminal is the terminal-handle type literal
a non-handle value is not a Terminal

column1: # §4  no backend registered → the first-class no_backend error. `open`

#     zero-arg overload would dispatch eagerly and silently swallow a
#     following options map (the P7 dispatch finding), so the bare

column3: open with options requires a registered backend

edit folds a key event into the input

column3: home then delete removes the character under the cursor
a non-key event leaves the input unchanged
the mask option rides the widget map (the renderer paints bullets)
